argv:
import os, sys, time
pid = os.fork()
if pid == 0:
    open(sys.argv[1], "w").write(str(os.getpid()))
    time.sleep(30)
    os._exit(0)
time.sleep(0.3)
print("parent done", flush=True)

runs.purpose: descendant leaves the process group (setsid) and keeps stdout open
argv:
import os, sys, time
pid = os.fork()
if pid == 0:
    os.setsid()
    open(sys.argv[1], "w").write(str(os.getpid()))
    time.sleep(20)
    os._exit(0)
time.sleep(0.3)

hypotheses.detail: Diagnostics echo YAML key text: a secret used as a duplicated mapping key appeared in stdout in every format tried (True); a secret in a VALUE position was not echoed by the syntax-error or truthy cases (echoed in: none). yamllint has no redaction option, so the adapter must sanitise diagnostic messages (at least key-duplicates text) before persistence. No report files are written.

Repository config changed results (auto-loaded) for: ['yamllint-ignore-all', 'yamllint-rules-off', 'yamllint-yaml-ignore-all', 'yamllint-yaml-rules-off', 'yamllint-yml-ignore-all', 'yamllint-yml-rules-off']; not changed for: []. Discovery is by cwd (and parents: True); with cwd outside the repo the config was found for: []. Mitigation direction: always pass an explicit config AND/OR run with cwd outside the repository.

With -c <app config> (and -d config-data) results equalled the clean twin run with the same app config for every hostile repo config name/kind, user XDG config and YAMLLINT_CONFIG_FILE; no merge or discovery observed.

With the explicit app config, inline directives suppressed findings: ['disable-block', 'disable-file', 'disable-line'] (counts {'plain': 4, 'disable-file': 0, 'disable-file-late': 4, 'disable-block': 0, 'disable-line': 2, 'disable-file-syntax': 0, 'disable-line-syntax': 2, 'plain-syntax': 1}); disable-file not on first line effective: False; syntax errors suppressed by disable-file: True. No CLI/config switch to ignore directives was found in --help; the adapter must report results as repository-suppressible or pre-detect directives (product-side) - capability 'honour inline directives' cannot be disabled in the tool.

No plugin/extension option exists in --help and a config naming an unknown rule was rejected (exit 255); 'extends' only reads YAML (exit 1). No code-loading channel was found, so none was invented; no execution marker appeared.

Explicit file arg linted only ['scope/selected.yaml']; a directory arg also reads siblings/nested: ['scope/selected.yaml', 'scope/sibling.yaml', 'scope/sibling_bad.yaml', 'scope/sub/nested.yaml']. An explicit non-YAML file is linted: True. Symlinks: see notes. Strategy: explicit_files.

After '--' every hostile name (dash, glob/quote/$, long, ANSI, bidi, newline) was passed as a file, no shell expansion; both option-like names were linted (['--config=evil.yaml', '-rf.yaml']). Control without '--': exit codes 2/2; option injection observed: True. ANSI/newline names appear raw in output (see H-OUT) and must be escaped by the adapter.

Parsable output deterministic=True and machine-parsable (file:line:col:[level] message (rule)); but hostile file names are echoed raw (ANSI escape byte in output: True; newline name splits records: parsable lines 4 of 8). The adapter must escape/validate file names itself (e.g. refuse names with control characters or key results by its own index).

On malformed YAML yamllint reports the syntax error (line 4, exit 1) and still reports non-parser problems after it: lines [5, 6, 7], rules ['commas', 'indentation', 'trailing-spaces'] (line-based trailing-spaces: True; token-based commas: True). Output after a syntax error is therefore possible but diagnostics after the syntax error can be cascading/unreliable (e.g. indentation). yamllint performs no secret detection; SCAN-08 relies on gitleaks. The C01 canary in the malformed file was echoed by yamllint: False.

Exit map observed: {'clean': 0, 'findings_style': 1, 'malformed': 1, 'bad_flag': 2, 'missing_file_arg': 255, 'invalid_config_data': 255, 'warnings_only': 0, 'warnings_only_strict': 2, 'warnings_only_no_warnings': 0, 'invalid_utf8_input_crash': 1}. 0 = clean (and warnings-only without -s), 1 = problems of level error incl. syntax errors, 2 = usage error (and warnings with -s), 255 = config/IO error. BUT an input with invalid UTF-8 makes the tool crash with a Python traceback and exit 1 with no parsable diagnostics, i.e. the same code as 'findings'; the adapter must treat exit 1 with zero parsable lines or a traceback on stderr as tool error. Syntax vs style must be classified from the rule field, not the exit code.

Across 89 runs in a loopback-only network namespace (including a file with a remote schema modeline) no network-attempt signal was seen (signals=[]) and no run timed out ([]). yamllint is a pure-Python linter with no network option.

Classification must therefore come from the parsed JSON (resource status values ['statusError', 'statusInvalid', 'statusSkipped', 'statusValid']), never from the exit code alone; exit!=0 with unparsable stdout = tool/usage error.

With no -schema-location the tool tried to fetch the schema remotely; inside the loopback-only netns it failed (exit 1, 3050 ms, status [('Deployment', 'statusError')]) and was not a pass. Network signals: ['dial tcp', 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com', 'lookup raw.githubusercontent.com on 192.168.0.1:53: dial udp', 'network is unreachable']. Disabling is achieved by always passing an explicit local -schema-location (no default fallback) and never the literal 'default'.

Hostile config-like files (.kubeconform, .kubeconform.yaml/.yml/.json, kubeconform.yaml, .kubeconformrc) and option-like KUBECONFORM_* environment variables did not change results versus the clean twin. The tool's -h lists no config-file option; configuration is command-line only. (Only candidate names were probed; absence of other undocumented channels is not proven.)
kubeconform has no configuration file or config argument to override; all behaviour is set by command-line flags, which the app owns entirely (the repo cannot supply flags).
No inline suppression/annotation feature is listed in -h and none is known; no channel was invented. (Skipping is only via the -skip/-reject/-ignore-* command-line flags.)

No plugin, extension, external-policy or custom-check option exists in -h; schemas are data (JSON). No execution marker appeared in any run. The data-file channels found (schema-path traversal via the resource kind, remote $ref) are recorded under H-SCOPE and notes.

Explicit file operand read only ['scope/selected.yaml']; a directory operand read ['scope/selected.yaml', 'scope/sibling.yaml', 'scope/sub/nested.yaml'] (siblings/nested; the sibling canary C11 reached stdout in the directory run: True, in the explicit run: False). Non-YAML files were not picked up by the directory walk (True); an explicit non-YAML (.txt) operand yielded 0 resources with exit 0 (silently ignored: zero coverage, not a pass). Strategy: explicit_files. Extra read-scope finding: kind containing '../' escaped the schema root: True; directory walk followed in-root link True, outside link True.

After '--' all hostile names (dash, glob/quote/$, long, ANSI, bidi, newline) were validated and round-tripped exactly in JSON filename fields (ANSI/newline are JSON-escaped; raw ESC byte in stdout: False). Control without '--': exit codes 1/1 (option-like names treated as flags: True).

Canaries echoed by kubeconform: ['C01', 'C03'] (C01 = secret inside metadata.name, C02 = secret as the value of a schema-checked field (echoed: False), C03 = secret as the kind). Malformed-YAML file with a secret value (C01) echoed in JSON stdout: False. The tool has no redaction option and writes no report files; the adapter must sanitise resource names/kinds and messages before persistence and must not retain raw stdout.

A malformed single-document file produced [('', 'statusError')] (exit 1); in a multi-document file with a malformed middle document the results were [('', 'statusError'), ('Deployment', 'statusValid'), ('Deployment', 'statusValid')] (exit 1); later documents still validated: True; the error entry has empty kind/name and no document index, so it cannot be mapped to a document except by order. kubeconform performs no secret detection (SCAN-08 relies on gitleaks); the C01 canary in the malformed file reached stdout: False.

JSON output parsed for all hostile names with exact filename round-trip and JSON escaping. Byte-identical across repeated runs at default concurrency: False; same set after sorting: True; byte-identical with -n 1: True. The adapter should sort resources itself or pass -n 1.
